Engineering and Managerial Economics:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Introduction and Basic Concepts Meaning, nature and scope of Economics; role of Engineering in Economics; Managerial Economics and its scope in an Engineering perspective. Demand analysis; law of demand; determinants of demand; price, income and cross elasticity of demand. Meaning, significance and methods of demand forecasting; law of supply; factors affecting supply; elasticity of supply. | 15 | CO1 / CO2
2 | Production Function and Cost Concept Production functions; concept of iso-quants; Law of Variable Proportion and Law of Returns to Scale; economies and diseconomies of scale. Cost concepts: overview of short-run and long-run cost curves; fixed cost, variable cost, average cost, marginal cost and opportunity cost. | 15 | CO2 / CO3
3 | Market Structure; National Income, Inflation and Business Cycle Perfect competition, imperfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, duopoly and salient features of price discrimination. Concept and measurement of national income; economic indicators; meaning, types, causes and prevention of inflation; phases of the business cycle. | 15 | CO3 / CO4
Microprocessor and Interfacing:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Introduction: Memory and Microprocessor Memory unit and primary memory: RAM, SRAM, DRAM, ROM, PROM, EPROM and EEPROM. Secondary memory: magnetic memory, tape and disk; cache memory; real and virtual memory; addressing capacity of CPU; evolution and types of microprocessors; microprocessor architecture and components; addressing modes; interrupts; data transfer schemes; instruction and data flow; timers and timing diagrams; interfacing devices; architectural advancements; typical microprocessor development schemes. | 30 | CO1
2 | 8085 Microprocessor 8-bit microprocessor: internal architecture; pin diagram; interrupts and machine cycle; instruction sets; addressing modes; instruction classification; machine control and assembler directives; technical features of Pentium, Pentium Pro, Pentium II, Pentium III and Pentium IV microprocessors. | 30 | CO2
3 | 8086 Microprocessor and Assembly Language Programming 16-bit microprocessor: 8086 architecture; register organization; bus interface unit; execution unit; memory addressing; operating modes; instruction sets, formats and types; 8086 family; procedures and macros; connection, timing and troubleshooting; interrupts. Assembly language programming based on Intel 8085/8086: data transfer, arithmetic, logic, branch operations, looping, counting, indexing, counters and time delays, stacks, subroutines, conditional calls and returns, debugging, modular and structured programming, top-down and bottom-up design, macro microprogramming. | 30 | CO3
4 | Peripheral Interfacing Introduction to peripheral devices; 8237 DMA controller; 8255 programmable peripheral interface; 8253/8254 programmable timer/counter; 8259 programmable interrupt controller; 8251 USART and RS232C. | 30 | CO4
Computer Networks:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Introduction and Physical Layer Network objectives and applications; network structure and architecture; OSI reference model; network services and standardization; network examples; TCP/IP model. Physical layer: fundamentals of data communication; transmission media; analog and digital transmission; switching; ISDN; terminal handling; broadcast channels and medium access; LAN protocols. | 30 | CO1
2 | Data Link Layer and Network Layer Data Link layer design issues; error detection and correction; elementary data-link protocols; sliding-window protocols and examples. Network layer design issues; routing algorithms; congestion control; internetworking; CSMA with collision detection; collision-free protocols; IEEE 802 LAN standards; comparison of LANs; fibre-optic network and FDDI. | 30 | CO2
3 | Transport, Session and Presentation Layers Transport layer design issues; connection management; example of a simple transport protocol. Session layer design issues; remote procedure call and examples. Presentation layer design issues; data compression and encryption; network security and privacy. | 30 | CO3 / CO4
4 | Application Layer Application-layer design issues; file transfer and file access; electronic mail; virtual terminals; other applications; case study based on available network software. | 30 | CO4
Automata Theory and Formal Languages:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Fundamentals and Finite Automata Formal languages, strings, alphabets, languages and Chomsky hierarchy. Finite-state machines; acceptance of strings and languages; deterministic finite automata (DFA) and non-deterministic finite automata (NFA); equivalence of NFA and DFA, including epsilon moves; minimization and equivalence of DFAs; automata with output; Moore and Mealy machines and conversions. | 30 | CO1
2 | Regular Languages and Context-Free Grammars Regular expressions and identity rules; conversion between regular expressions and finite automata; pumping lemma and closure properties of regular sets. Context-free grammars and languages; derivation trees; leftmost/rightmost derivations and sentential forms; ambiguity; left recursion and left factoring; minimization; Chomsky and Greibach normal forms; pumping lemma for context-free languages; closure and decision properties. | 30 | CO2
3 | Pushdown Automata Introduction to pushdown automata; acceptance of context-free languages by final state and by empty state; equivalence of context-free grammars and pushdown automata; inter-conversion. | 30 | CO3
4 | Turing Machine (TM) Problems that computers cannot solve; Turing machine and programming techniques; extensions and restricted Turing machines; Turing machines and computers; Post’s Correspondence Problem; a language that is not recursively enumerable; an undecidable problem that is recursively enumerable; context-sensitive languages and Chomsky hierarchy; other undecidable problems. | 30 | CO4
Computer Graphics:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Introduction to Computer Graphics, Graphic Displays, Line and Circle Drawing Algorithms Types of computer graphics; random-scan and raster-scan displays; frame buffer and video controller; points and lines; line-drawing algorithms; circle-generating algorithms; midpoint circle algorithm and parallel versions. | 30 | CO1
2 | Transformations, Windowing and Clipping Basic transformations; matrix representations and homogeneous coordinates; composite transformations, reflections and shearing. Viewing pipeline and viewing transformations. 2D clipping: Cohen-Sutherland and Liang-Barsky line-clipping algorithms; line clipping against non-rectangular windows; Sutherland-Hodgman and Weiler-Atherton polygon clipping; curve and text clipping. | 30 | CO2
3 | 3D Transformation Three-dimensional geometric primitives and object representation; 3D transformations and viewing; projections; 3D clipping. | 30 | CO3 / CO4
4 | Curves and Surfaces, Hidden Lines and Surfaces, Basic Illumination Model Quadric surfaces, spheres, ellipsoids and blobby objects; introductory spline, B-spline and Bezier curves and surfaces. Back-face detection, depth-buffer method, A-buffer method and scan-line method. Basic illumination models: ambient light, diffuse reflection, specular reflection and Phong model. | 30 | CO3 / CO4
Essence of Indian Traditional Knowledge:
Module | Module / Course Contents | Contact Hours | Mapped CO
1 | Introduction to Traditional Knowledge Introduction to Indian Traditional Knowledge: concept, significance, historical background and evolution in India. Intellectual Property Rights (IPR): overview and importance for traditional knowledge; copyright, trademarks, patents and geographical indications. Traditional Knowledge and Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs): protection challenges and international frameworks such as the WIPO Intergovernmental Committee on Intellectual Property and Genetic Resources, Traditional Knowledge and Folklore. Traditional Knowledge and Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK): relationship, role in environmental conservation and sustainable development. | 30 | CO1 / CO2
2 | Traditional Knowledge and IPR Laws in India Traditional Knowledge and IPR laws: legal framework in India and relevant laws/regulations such as the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL). Traditional Knowledge and Patent Law: challenges, issues and case studies. Traditional Knowledge and Copyright Law: cultural appropriation and protection of traditional expressions. Traditional Knowledge and Geographical Indications (GI): significance and case studies on registration/protection of traditional products and practices. Traditional Knowledge, IPR and the Future: trends and prospects, digital platforms and traditional-knowledge dissemination. | 30 | CO3 / CO4
